body.statement: Under Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass:star-iid-superpopulation}\) and \(\mathrm{ass:star-complete-randomization}\), the randomized balanced subsample in Definition \(\mathrm{def:star-transformation}\) satisfies \(\mathcal L((X_{ki}^{\mathrm{STAR}})_{1\le k\le3,1\le i\le36})=\bigotimes_{k=1}^3(P_k^{\mathrm{STAR}})^{\otimes36}\). It therefore has \(N=108\), \(K=3\), \(m=36\), and \(d=5\), and \(\inf_{\gamma\in\Gamma(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})}\mathbb E_\gamma\|\sum_{k=1}^3Z_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}\|_2^2=9L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})\). Consequently, \(9b_Y^2L(\mathbf P^{\mathrm{STAR}})\) is the sharp lower endpoint for \(\mathbb E[(\sum_{k=1}^3\beta_k^{\mathrm{STAR}}Y(k))^2]\). This empirical audit is conditional on the declared i.i.d. superpopulation law, the known bound \(B^{\mathrm{STAR}}\), the affine scaling, complete randomization, and randomized balanced subsampling; it does not validate the native-count \((161,37,36)\) plug-in calculation.
body.justification: The audit separates the estimand-preserving scale transformation from the sampling contract actually required by the theory.
body.gap: Gao--Ge--Qian's theoretical display is balanced, while its public STAR computation uses native unequal cell sizes and does not supply this known-bound scaling plus superpopulation-to-product-law reduction.
body.consumer: A reanalysis of the scholarship-incentive contrast can state exactly which observations, scale, and endpoint its guarantee covers.
